fills.researcher_notes: Punj Lloyd's own 25-years retrospective (Yumpu-hosted company publication, p.56, verified live, contains 'Melita') states the government set a target for Punj Lloyd to commission the Tripoli-Melita gas pipeline early, 'charging gas from Melita to Zawia Power Plant by March 2010,' and that 'Punj Lloyd achieved this target.' A 2020 Libya Herald article (verified live, contains 'Punj Lloyd') on Sirte Oil's successful defense of an ICC arbitration brought by Punj Lloyd corroborates that Punj Lloyd built a Sirte-Oil-contracted gas pipeline in this corridor and that construction/completion was disrupted around the 2011 revolution period. Tier medium rather than high: the two sources are not fully independent in origin (Punj Lloyd's own retrospective is a primary-but-self-interested account; Libya Herald corroborates the contractor/project relationship and dispute but does not itself restate the March 2010 commissioning date). No second, fully independent outlet was found stating the exact 2010 date before WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session.

validity.recommendation: Do not adopt a corrected LengthKnownKm for this length_ratio flag from route evidence alone. No source found names a distinct, standalone ~25 km 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline; the sourced project in this corridor (Punj Lloyd's Tripoli-Melita/Zawia gas link, above) instead reads as the same corridor already covered end-to-end by P1864 Khoms-Tripoli + P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (WB/Tractebel corroborated combined length ~222 km, Mellitah-Tripoli-Khoms). The drawn 250 km geometry for P1789 traces essentially that same Khoms-to-Mellitah coastline, not a short local 25 km spur. This is consistent with (but does not resolve or re-decide) the already-staged redundancy-pass finding that P1789 may duplicate P1864+P1865 — flagging only the length_ratio evidence here, per the brief's instruction not to re-litigate the duplication verdict itself.
